source: Morais O., Cargill C., Parke K. and Barnes T. 2020. Smallholder Pig Production Technicians' Manual. Timor-Leste Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries, University of Queensland, ACIAR and the TOMAK Program (Australian Aid), Dili.
text: Do not use a boar for mating before he is 10 months old — younger boars have lower sperm quality, which can also reduce his fertility later in life. A boar should mate at least 2–3 sows per week but no more than once per day; using him every second day works well. Farmers with only 3–5 sows should consider sharing a boar with neighbouring farmers so he gets enough matings to stay fertile. House the boar in a pen with access to an outside yard planted with high-protein pasture grass and fodder trees for foraging. Feed him ad-lib unless he becomes fat (a fat boar may have reduced libido), and always provide clean water.
caveat: This guidance comes from a Timor-Leste smallholder pig manual, not a Cambodia-specific source. Feed ingredients and general husbandry practices transfer well to Cambodia's tropical smallholder conditions, but local breed weights/ages and disease-context details may differ; confirm specifics with a local vet or extension officer where precision matters.
